primary_claim: Applying solid-state-physics phonon/boundary-condition theory to word-embedding co-occurrence statistics correctly predicts the geometric shape (circular for periodic/cyclic concepts, parabolic for open-ended ordinal scales, mixed Dirichlet-Neumann sinusoidal for logarithmic scales, and product-of-cosines for 2D concepts like the valence-arousal emotion circumplex) of how GloVe and Gemma (2B, 27B) represent semantic concepts in their embedding/activation principal-component space.

effect.metric: R^2 of geometric fit (circle/parabola/sinusoid/product-cosine) to PCA-projected embeddings
effect.value: periodic concepts in Gemma 2B: months R^2 at layer 12 (55.6% variance), days layer 5 (53.5%), compass layer 7 (32.3%); Neumann ordinal concepts fit predicted parabola (e.g. quality R^2 at layer 18, 29.1% variance); log-scale concepts fit predicted sinusoid (e.g. time layer 9, 34.5%); 2D Neumann on 69 emotion words in Gemma 2 27B layer 28: valence mode R^2=0.86, valence-arousal interaction mode R^2=0.67

stated_future_work: extend the phonon picture to additional boundary condition types
study how different modes might interfere with one another and what such interference would mean
explore whether a principled geometric understanding of concepts like morality or harm could offer a path toward understanding and enforcing alignment
limitations_stated: the theory holds exactly only in the full-rank regime, where embedding dimension is at least as large as the rank of the PMI matrix; GloVe at d=300 with 400k vocabulary is far from this regime, giving noisier results
storage concept in Gemma 2B was the weakest case: the best-matching principal component captured essentially no variance
the lattice-structure connection to the Lattice Representation Hypothesis paper is explicitly noted as speculative
much more work is needed to establish how robust and general these patterns are
quote: I tested whether this connection extends beyond a single case by applying different boundary conditions to different semantic concepts, and found confirmation for periodic, Neumann, mixed, and 2D Neumann geometries.
